name: CuspAI
description: CuspAI is privately held and has no ticker. Review its funding rounds and valuations, its investors, and the points to confirm before buying or selling.
ledes: CuspAI is a privately held artificial intelligence company focused on materials science. Its shares are not listed on an exchange and have no quoted market price; the principal public reference points are the valuations at which the company has raised capital. Its most recent financing, a $450 million Series B round announced on July 20, 2026, was reported to value the company at $2.6 billion.

Founded in 2024 and based in Cambridge, England, CuspAI develops AI software that designs and screens candidate materials, such as compounds for carbon capture and semiconductor manufacturing, for industrial customers. Existing shares change hands in privately negotiated transactions and remain subject to the company's transfer restrictions.
table_note: Valuations are as reported at the time of each round. CuspAI declined to comment on its Series A valuation, which was reported by Fortune.
round_notes: Kleiner Perkins and NEA co-led the Series B, with significant participation from Bezos Expeditions. Alongside the round, CuspAI launched the AI Materials Foundry, a network that it said had more than 45 founding members in July 2026, including Nvidia, Meta and Samsung.

A round valuation reflects the terms of the preferred stock issued in that round. Most shares sold by employees are common stock, which carries fewer rights and typically trades at a discount to the preferred price.
investors: Kleiner Perkins and NEA co-led the Series B, with participation from Bezos Expeditions, Lux Capital, AMD Ventures, Glade Brook Capital Partners, StepStone, Invest-NL and Britain's Sovereign AI Venture Fund. NEA and Temasek co-led the Series A, and Hoxton Ventures led the seed round. Other investors include Lightspeed Venture Partners, Basis Set Ventures, Northzone, LocalGlobe, Nvidia's venture arm NVentures, Samsung Ventures and Hyundai Motor Group.
spv_sentence: No special purpose vehicles naming CuspAI appear in SEC Form D filings.
sources: Sources: reports by SiliconANGLE (July 2026), UKTN (July 2026), Fortune (September 2025) and TechCrunch (June 2024); and SEC Form D filings.
